competitorWins: World Monitor is genuinely stronger for dedicated defense and geopolitical analysis. Its six specialized variants (geopolitical, tech, finance, energy, commodity), 200+ mapped military bases, 26 Telegram OSINT channels, Country Instability Index, and AI strategic-posture panels go far deeper into military intelligence than WorldEye's Pro conflict feeds. Being open-source and self-hosted, it has no subscription cost and can be customized by a technical team.
description: World Monitor (worldmonitor.app) is an open-source, self-hosted platform built for OSINT analysts, defense researchers, and journalists. It ships six specialized variants — geopolitical, tech, finance, energy, commodity, and positive-news — and combines live ADS-B aircraft tracking, AIS maritime monitoring, military base maps, Telegram OSINT channels, a Country Instability Index, and GDELT-powered news feeds. It differs from WorldEye by targeting deep defense/geopolitical analysis (you self-host the open-source code) rather than a free, no-signup consumer globe with cameras, weather, and affordable Pro extras.

seoDescription: Compare WorldEye vs World Monitor: free no-signup planet globe with cameras and Pro OSINT extras vs open-source self-hosted geopolitical intelligence.
seoTitle: WorldEye vs World Monitor (2026): Free Live Globe or Open-Source Intel Platform?
tagline: Open-source geopolitical intelligence platform with 100+ intel panels for military tracking, conflict monitoring, and AI-driven analysis.
verdictCompetitor: Choose World Monitor if you are an OSINT analyst, defense researcher, or journalist who needs deep military and geopolitical intelligence panels and are comfortable self-hosting open-source software.
verdictWorldEye: Choose WorldEye if you want a free, no-signup live planet globe — cameras, flights, ships, weather, quakes — plus affordable Pro OSINT extras, without hosting anything yourself.
whyWorldEye: Free in your browser with zero signup — World Monitor requires you to deploy and host the open-source stack yourself.
One free globe combines ~36,000 live public cameras with live flights, ships, weather, earthquakes, and wildfires — World Monitor has no camera network.
Pro starts at $3.99/week: AI analyst assistant, OSINT recon toolkit (Nmap, DNS, WHOIS, SSL), premium cyber/GDELT/maritime/conflict intel feeds, and high-res satellite imagery.
Free live aircraft, satellite, and ship tracking with global search and advanced filters — no account, no infrastructure.
A mobile-friendly 3D globe designed for anyone to explore the planet, not just defense analysts.
WorldEye's GDELT-powered intel feeds complement World Monitor's deeper military panels — use them together.
